page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It features 64 virtual CPUs, corresponding to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory, translating to a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 61947.26 and a PassMark CPU score of 56826.42. The instance demonstrates strong performance in database operations, scoring 26144.88 on PassMark, and shows average performance in Redis SET operations at 55.61 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests show average results, reaching 3352.15 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 153.34 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing benchmarks also register in the strong tier.

Given its massive memory footprint and local NVMe storage, the x2iedn.16xlarge is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data-intensive enterprise applications. While it lacks dedicated GPU hardware, it achieves strong performance in small-to-medium LLM inference tasks, such as text generation with a 7B model. The high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation offer qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require massive RAM capacity without the overhead of scaling out to multiple smaller instances.
